_description: MJ Tonnerre campaign TEMPLATE — COPY this folder (_template) for each new campaign, then fill in the empty fields. Structure aligned with real campaigns (example-mistfall) and conforming to scripts/schemas/world.schema.json. Key sections: meta (identity + time + features), system (base rules), modules (thematic toggles), rules (time/movements), global_state (living factions), universe (regions + locations). Location id convention: 'lieu:<region-slug>/<location-slug>' (sub-location: 'lieu:<region-slug>/<parent-slug>/<location-slug>') — geo_query.py derives containment from this hierarchical id. A 'geo_query build' on this template must succeed (worst case: 0 edges): never commit geo.json in _template.

time._note: regime = type of time tracking. 'Narrative' (GM estimates durations) OR 'UT' (strict Time Units, e.g. 1 UT = 10 min, 144 UT/day). 'tracking' holds the start point (day/hour) — see also rules.time.tracking.

features._schema: Five main ON/OFF axes of the game engine, ALL true by default. Resolution cascade: meta.features.<axis> (here) > env MGM_FEATURE_<AXIS> (instance default at deployment) > true. world.json has the final word. All effects are fail-open: an ON axis whose data is missing (e.g. temporality without geo.json/actors.json) is a no-op, never an error. Details: docs/monde-vivant/10-features.md. — traceability: CSV journal collecte.csv + git auto-commit + session snapshots. verbosity: "Persisted" block from the Steward + meta.verbosity level. living_npcs_factions: factions/npc_proactivity modules + actors that "think" (world_tick). temporality: living world engine (world_tick pre/post, scene brief, causal propagation). images: mygamemaster-images skill.

meta._pj_ids: actor ids of PCs, e.g. ["acteur:name"] ; the engine links 'towards-player' relationships to these ids. Keep [] until PCs are created.

audio._note: TTS voice config. 'voice' and 'language_boost' override the per-language default set by meta.langue (or env MGM_LANGUAGE). Omit both to let the engine choose automatically. See modules/gaming/mygamemaster-tts/SKILL.md § Voice selection.

system._note: Minimal game system — adapt stats/resolution to the campaign. crunch 1 (very light) to 5 (very technical).
system.name: d20 narrative
system.resolution: d20 + stat modifier (+ skill bonus if applicable) ≥ DC (10 easy, 15 medium, 20 hard)
system.nat20: Critical success — the best possible outcome for the situation
system.nat1: Critical failure — the worst possible outcome for the situation
system.skills: Bonus of +3 (proficient) on d20 based on specialization
system.health: Hit Points (HP) — HP = 10 + Constitution modifier at level 1
system.combat: Simple and narrative — no grid, focus on choice and consequence

modules._schema: Each module is loaded/applied by the main skill only if actif==true (pattern following meta.time.regime). params={} = module default values; override here to adjust without touching the skill. See skills/gaming/mygamemaster/references/modules/README.md

time.principe: Narrative time — the GM announces durations and advances the clock in blocks. Adapt if the campaign switches to strict UT (see meta.time.regime).

rules: These durations are fixed — modifying a route = breaking map coherence
Any new route must be coherent with existing ones: indirect ≥ direct
Durations are one-way trips (round-trip = duration × 2). 1 day's march = 12h of daylight
A distant point cannot be reachable in less time than a nearby neighbor point
gouvernance.verification: Before adding a route: verify the 4 rules above + compare with neighboring routes
gouvernance.procedure: Whenever I describe a new journey in the narration (distance or estimated duration), I record the route IMMEDIATELY in world.json → rules.time.movements BEFORE writing the rest. Never close the narrative response without the route being committed.

movements._exemple_route: EXAMPLE route to copy (key then value): "from_<location-a>_to": { "<location-b>": "40min — westward, follow the stream to the embankment, climb the embankment" }. geo_query reads the duration (40min) and direction (west) from this description and derives an edge. Labels (<location-a>, <location-b>) are resolved to ids via the name/alias of universe.regions locations.

tracking._note: Current position in the game timeline — update at each session.

rules: Each faction ALWAYS has at least 1 short-term action (deadline ≤ 7 days) and 1 long-term action (deadline ≥ 14 days) in its actions_en_cours
Objectives (short and long term in the 'factions' section) are INDEPENDENT of PCs — they exist and evolve even if PCs never intervene
When a short-term objective is achieved, exceeded, or superseded → renew it immediately with a new objective, coherent with the long term
PCs can encounter these actions (endure them, observe them, influence them) but NOT cancel them — an action that becomes impossible transforms, does not disappear
gouvernance.renouvellement: At the start of each session: check every faction. If its short-term objective is moot → replace it.

regions.name: Example Region
regions.description: Example region to replace. The id 'region:<slug>' is the containment root: all locations belonging to it encode its slug in their own id ('lieu:exemple/...').

locations.name: Example Location
locations.description: Example location to replace. Id convention: 'lieu:<region-slug>/<location-slug>' (here region-slug='exemple'). For a sub-location (a room in this location): 'lieu:exemple/lieu-dexemple/<sub-location-slug>'. The 'alias' field lists short names used in rules.time.movements to link routes to this location.
